ground_truth_root_cause: The Kubernetes namespace ResourceQuota for frontend-ns had its pod hard limit set to 4 in commit b72e4d9 (infra/k8s/namespaces/frontend-ns/resource-quota.yaml). Although commit e91c3a6 correctly raised the HPA maxReplicas to 12, the namespace-level ResourceQuota was never updated to match. When the marketing campaign triggered a 4x traffic spike at 13:00 UTC, the HPA attempted to schedule 8 additional pods, but all were blocked by the ResourceQuota hard limit of 4 pods. The cluster had ample physical capacity (35%+ free CPU and RAM across all nodes), but the misconfigured quota prevented any scale-out, causing the existing 4 pods to become overwhelmed, leading to OOMKills and a 91%+ HTTP 503 error rate.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately patch the ResourceQuota to allow sufficient pods: kubectl patch resourcequota frontend-ns -n frontend-ns -p with hard pods limit set to 20. 2. Verify pending pods are now scheduled and become Running. 3. Confirm HPA scales to desired replica count and error rate normalizes. 4. Long-term: add a CI/CD policy check that ensures HPA maxReplicas never exceeds namespace ResourceQuota pod limits, and require both to be updated together. 5. Update the resource-quota.yaml in version control to reflect the corrected limit and conduct a full audit of all namespace quotas before future planned campaigns.
